summary.text: 边 is the simplified form of 邊. It names an object’s outer edge, a geographic boundary, or a side or nearby position. In 一边…一边…, it links simultaneous actions, often translated “while.” The early construction of 邊 remains disputed.

formation.text: 边 is the simplified form of 邊. In current 邊, 辶 represents 辵, whose movement meaning is assigned in cited analyses. The main formation account assigns the sound role to 臱; separate accounts name 𦤝 or propose roles for 自, 丙, and 方 in early forms. Another account proposes an oracle-form analysis in which 自 represents the original graph of 鼻 and 丙 supplies sound. These are distinct, disputed analyses; the early construction remains unresolved. In 边, 力 replaces the elaborate right-hand 臱 of 邊 and does not thereby inherit its proposed sound role.

components.text: In 边, 辶 is the left-side positional form of 辵. The cited movement contribution belongs to 邊; its continuation in 边 is probable, not certain.
In 边, the right-hand 力 replaces the elaborate 臱 form in 邊. 力 does not inherit 臱’s proposed sound role.
In 邊, 辶 is the left-side positional form of 辵. One analysis assigns 辵 a movement contribution; the separate main account identifies 臱 as the sound element. Other early analyses differ.
The Han-era Shuowen account identifies 𦤝 as 邊’s sound element. Its graphic identity is not established as the same as 臱 in the separate account.

sound_limitation.text: The Zhengzhang reconstruction comparison 臱 *men and 邊 *mpeːn concerns 臱, not 𦤝. Since their graphic identity is not established, it cannot validate 𦤝’s proposed sound role.

components.text: The main formation account assigns the sound role to 臱 in 邊. A separate analysis of an oracle form proposes 自 as 鼻’s original graph and 丙 as a sound element. These are distinct accounts; their referents and roles are not established as identical.

sound_limitation.text: The Zhengzhang comparison supports a reported sound comparison between 臱 and 邊. It does not establish that 臱 is graphically identical with Shuowen’s 𦤝 or settle which analysis is preferable.

sound.text: The Zhengzhang Old Chinese comparison records 臱 *men and 邊 *mpeːn in the same reconstruction system; it is a source-reported comparison, not proof of the preferred analysis.
The current Mandarin readings are 臱 mián and 邊 biān; this modern comparison does not establish the historical sound role.

components.text: One analysis of the bronze form assigns 方 the meaning “beside”; a competing analysis assigns meaning to 辵.

The bronze-form proposal assigns 自 a sound role and 方 the sense “beside”; a separate oracle-form proposal describes 自 as 鼻’s original graph. These are distinct analyses, and the proposed sound role is not established by the available readings.

sound_limitation.text: No comparable ancient readings for 自 and 邊 in the proposed early analysis were established. The available current Mandarin readings do not establish that historical sound relationship.

sound.text: The current Mandarin readings are 自 zì and 邊 biān; they differ and do not establish an ancient sound match.

components.text: The bronze-form proposal assigns 丙 a sound role; a separate oracle-form proposal also treats 丙 as sound-bearing. Its Mandarin reading bǐng differs from 邊 biān and does not establish the proposed historical role.

sound_limitation.text: No comparable ancient readings for 丙 and 邊 in the proposed early analysis were established. The available current Mandarin readings do not establish that historical sound relationship.

sound.text: The current Mandarin readings are 丙 bǐng and 邊 biān; they differ and do not establish an ancient sound match.

uncertainties.text: The main formation analysis assigns movement meaning to 辵 and sound to 臱. The Han-era Shuowen account assigns sound to 𦤝; a bronze-form proposal assigns “beside” to 方 and sound roles to 自 and 丙. The scanned account separately proposes an oracle-form analysis in which 自 represents the original graph of 鼻 and 丙 supplies sound. The evidence does not settle which account best explains the early graph.
One account calls 臱 the original graph, but whether it directly precedes 邊 or the earliest form was already 邊 remains unresolved.

The Zhengzhang comparison records 臱 *men and 邊 *mpeːn, while the Han-era account assigns a sound role specifically to 𦤝. The sources do not establish that these are the same graph. The proposed sound roles for 自 and 丙 also lack a supporting ancient reading pair in the cited analyses; current readings do not establish those historical roles.

The selected redraws do not establish a graphic sequence: the oracle- and bronze-style examples are not tied to specific dated artifacts, and the cited silk manuscript image is not examined in the file description.

senses.text: 边 names the surrounding part or outer edge of an object.
边 can name the boundary between countries or regions.
边 can mean a side or a nearby position.

senses.gloss: while, in the paired construction 一边…一边…
senses.text: In 一边…一边…, 边 helps link two actions performed by the same subject at the same time, often translated as “while.” The history of this construction and its relation to spatial senses are unresolved.

limitations.text: One analysis proposes “beside” as an original sense of 邊, but this is a proposal rather than an independently established use; its date and status as the original meaning remain unresolved. Separately, a database reports a bronze-inscription use of 邊 for a frontier region and a place-name 邊柳. The artifact readings were not independently checked, so these remain reported historical readings rather than verified attestations. Neither report establishes a dated sequence or continuity with current 边 senses.

relationships.text: One analysis of 邊 treats 辶, the left-side form of 辵, as contributing movement meaning; analyses of the early graph differ.
The Han-era account identifies 𦤝 as the sound element of 邊; the corrected book account names 臱, and the sources do not establish that the two referents are graphically identical.

The main formation account assigns sound to 臱 in 邊 and separately reports a Zhengzhang comparison for 臱 and 邊. This does not establish that 臱 is graphically identical with the distinct 𦤝 named in the Shuowen account, or which analysis is preferable.
One analysis of the bronze form assigns 方 the meaning “beside,” differing from the movement-based account of 辵.
Some analyses propose that 自 marks sound in early 邊, but comparable ancient readings for 自 in this character were not established.
Some analyses propose that 丙 marks sound in early 邊, but comparable ancient readings for 丙 in this character were not established.

For current 边, 辶 is the positional form of 辵. The current dictionary analysis assigns 辵 a meaning role, and the inspected formation account says 辵 contributes meaning in 邊 while 力 replaces its elaborate right-hand 臱 in 边. This supports a probable continuation of 辵’s semantic role, not an established ancient-to-current lineage.

overview.text: 边 is the simplified form of 邊. It can mean an object’s outer edge, a geographic boundary, or a side or nearby position. In 一边…一边…, it links simultaneous actions, often “while.” Its current form has 辶 and 力.

components.text: 辶 is the left-side form of 辵. Its movement contribution is described for 邊; continuity of that role in 边 is probable, not certain.
力 is 边’s visible right-hand part. It replaces 邊’s elaborate 臱, but does not inherit 臱’s proposed sound role.

limitations.text: No glyph is shown because the oracle-style redraw is not tied to a specific dated artifact, so it cannot document a securely dated specimen or resolve the competing analyses of 邊’s early components and their roles.
